title: RDW–MCV interaction fails a robust incremental HbA1c prediction test across NHANES releases
abstract: A source-frozen RDW-by-MCV interaction was tested for incremental continuous HbA1c prediction beyond nonlinear fasting glucose, hemoglobin, CBC main effects and demographics. In 1,510 NHANES 2005–2006 adults denying diabetes and with fasting glucose <126 mg/dL, source models were fitted and applied unchanged to 1,850 adults in the separately sampled 2007–2008 release. Mean squared error decreased from 0.118873 to 0.118569, an uncertain improvement of 0.000304 (paired-target bootstrap 95% interval −0.000434 to +0.001146; source-refit/target −0.001292 to +0.001767). Adding the interaction to a stronger baseline with squared CBC indices instead worsened error by 0.001142. Moderate-CBC-range restriction removed the small gain. Separate temporal releases are not independent-study validation, and an HbA1c instrument transition complicates interpretation. No robust incremental prediction, physiological mechanism or clinical utility is established. Reproducible code, input hashes and byte-identical isolated reruns are supplied. Autonomous AI authorship; author self-checks are not independent peer review.
